categories.main_business_segments: Sarepta Therapeutics operates as a single business segment focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of RNA-targeted therapeutics, gene therapies, and other genetic medicines for rare diseases. Its primary commercial products are for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (Duchenne), and it is advancing a pipeline targeting limb-girdle muscular dystrophies (LGMDs), other neuromuscular disorders, and central nervous system (CNS) diseases.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer (PMO)-based exon-skipping RNA therapeutics and adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapies. Manufacturing is conducted through a hybrid model: Sarepta develops proprietary chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) capabilities for process optimization, but relies on specialized contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs) for GMP production and supply of both PMO and gene therapy products.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Sarepta’s primary customers are specialty pharmacies, specialty distributors, hospitals, and infusion centers that serve patients with rare neuromuscular diseases, especially Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The end markets are patients (primarily children) with genetically confirmed mutations amenable to Sarepta’s therapies, as well as healthcare providers and payors involved in rare disease treatment.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s main commercial market is the United States, where all four approved products are marketed. Sarepta also distributes products through early access programs in select countries outside the U.S., including Israel, Libya, Georgia, and Kuwait, and has partnered with Roche for commercialization of ELEVIDYS and potentially other products outside the U.S.
categories.supply_chain_position: Sarepta operates downstream in the biopharmaceutical supply chain, focusing on late-stage development, regulatory approval, commercialization, and distribution of finished therapeutics. It outsources most large-scale GMP manufacturing to third-party CMOs and distributes products through specialty pharmacy and distributor networks.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic priorities are to expand its gene therapy and RNA-targeted platforms, advance a diversified pipeline in rare neuromuscular and CNS diseases, and invest in next-generation precision genetic medicines. R&D initiatives include internal research, strategic collaborations (e.g., with Arrowhead for siRNA programs), and ongoing clinical trials to expand indications and verify clinical benefit for approved products.
categories.revenue_model: Sarepta generates revenue primarily through product sales of its approved therapies (EXONDYS 51, VYONDYS 53, AMONDYS 45, and ELEVIDYS), contract manufacturing and supply agreements (notably with Roche for ex-U.S. supply), and royalties from out-licensed products. Collaboration and milestone payments also contribute, but product sales are the main revenue driver.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Sarepta faces competition from pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies developing therapies for Duchenne and related neuromuscular diseases, including Nippon Shinyaku (Viltepso), Wave Life Sciences, Dyne Therapeutics, Avidity Biosciences, PepGen, BioMarin, Solid Biosciences, and others. Sarepta is a leader in Duchenne therapies, with first-to-market status for several exon-skipping drugs and the first approved gene therapy for Duchenne in the U.S.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Sarepta reported net revenues of $1.79 billion, up 56% from $1.14 billion in 2023, driven by the launch and expanded approval of ELEVIDYS. The company achieved net income of $235 million in 2024, reversing prior years’ losses, and ended the year with $1.5 billion in cash and investments. Sarepta has demonstrated rapid revenue growth, particularly with new product launches, and continues to invest heavily in R&D.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Sarepta’s value proposition centers on addressing high unmet medical needs in rare, life-threatening neuromuscular diseases with innovative, precision genetic medicines. Its products are differentiated by proprietary exon-skipping and gene therapy platforms, first-in-class or best-in-class status, and the ability to target specific genetic mutations, offering hope for conditions with limited or no other treatment options.
